title: Jordan strikes Syria after the church attack
lines: Jordan has launched air strikes inside Syria, days after a deadly attack on a church in Karak.
The attack on a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church killed at least nine people.
On Monday evening, Jordan's armed forces said they struck hideouts of armed groups in southern Syria.
Syrian civil defence says at least four sites were hit, in Deraa and Suweyda provinces.
It says seven people were killed, including a woman and three children from one family, in a tent at Al-Tai.
Jordan said the strikes were coordinated with the Syrian government.
But Syria denies this. It called the operation a treacherous attack, carried out without notice, and opened an investigation.
Syria has also closed the Nassib crossing, its only passenger and cargo crossing with Jordan.
In Jordan, security forces arrested three suspects in connection with the church attack, after a three-hour shootout.
King Abdullah has promised the harshest penalties for those responsible.
The strikes add a new front of tension, in a region already shaken by the war with Iran.
